name: Centro Historico (Parque Central & Cathedral)
tagline: The colonial heart around the yellow cathedral
description: Granada's historic core clusters around Parque Central and the landmark yellow cathedral, ringed by pastel colonial facades, churches, hotels and cafes. It is the most walkable, atmospheric and convenient part of town, putting markets, restaurants and daily life within a few flat blocks.
bestFor: First-timers and nomads who want everything within walking distance
pros: Close to cafes, markets and services
cons: Rentals near the plaza cost more

name: Calle La Calzada
tagline: The pedestrian restaurant and bar strip to the lake
description: La Calzada is Granada's famous colourful strip running from the cathedral toward the lakefront, packed with restaurants, bars, street tables and evening live music. It is the social and nightlife spine of town, sociable and fun, though the constant activity means it is lively well into the night.
bestFor: Nomads who want dining, nightlife and a buzzing street scene
pros: Best concentration of restaurants and bars
Short walk to both plaza and lakefront

name: Lakefront (Complejo Turistico & Las Isletas)
tagline: Waterside gateway to Lake Nicaragua and the Isletas
description: At the eastern edge of town, the Complejo Turistico lines the shore of Lake Cocibolca, where boats depart to explore the Isletas de Granada archipelago. It is a greener, more open, breezier zone of waterfront restaurants and docks, a short walk or ride from the centre down La Calzada.
bestFor: Those drawn to lake views, boat trips and open space
pros: Direct access to Las Isletas boat trips

name: Xalteva (quieter residential barrio)
tagline: Historic, calmer neighbourhood west of the centre
description: Just west of Parque Central around the Xalteva church and park, this older residential barrio is quieter and more local than the tourist strip, while still an easy walk into the historic core. It suits longer-stay nomads wanting calmer streets and a more everyday Nicaraguan feel.
bestFor: Long-stay nomads wanting calm and lower prices near the centre
cons: More Spanish needed day to day
